texto: With **so** + adjective or adjective + **dass** it is said that something is so strong that it has consequences: **Es regnet so stark, dass wir zu Hause bleiben** (it rains so much that we stay at home). The prayer with «dass» goes behind, with the verb at the end.
With «so» in front and the final verb: **so stark, dass**. Eye: do not confuse with the «dass» opinion of lesson 14.

**Sodass** means «so that» and links a consequence with a complete prayer: **Der Kurs war voll, sodass alle gehen mussten** (the course was full, so they all had to go). **Daher** (so) goes as «deshalb»: the verb goes in second position: **Er ist krank, daher bleibt er zu Hause**.

filas: Es ist so kalt, dass ich friere.
Der Kurs war voll, sodass alle gehen mussten.
Er ist krank, daher bleibt er zu Hause.

frases.de: Es ist so kalt, dass ich friere.
frases.es: Hace tanto frío que tengo frío.

frases.de: Der Kurs war voll, sodass wir zu Hause trainiert haben.
frases.es: El curso estaba lleno, así que entrenamos en casa.
frases.en: The course was full, so we trained at home.

frases.de: Mein Partner hat Geduld. Daher kommt er immer pünktlich.
frases.es: Mi pareja tiene paciencia. Por eso llega siempre puntual.
frases.en: My partner has patience. That's why he always comes on time.

bloques.pregunta: What connector does «so that» (a consequence) mean?
How do you say «So cold I'm cold»?

bloques.frase: Es regnet so stark, dass wir zu Hause bleiben.

opciones.texto: It's raining so much that we stay home.
It's raining because we're staying home.
It's raining, even if we stay home.

bloques.frase: Er ist krank, ___ bleibt er zu Hause.

opciones.explicacion: daher = that's why (verb in second position).

bloques.pregunta: What is the logical consequence of this situation?
bloques.frase: Der Kurs war voll, sodass alle gehen mussten.

opciones.texto: The course room completed its entire capacity, so the attendees had to withdraw.
opciones.explicacion: «sodass» introduces the consecutive consequence subordinated to the modal verb at the end.

opciones.texto: The course had free places, so that everyone could enrol without delay.
opciones.explicacion: It states otherwise: the classroom was fully full («voll»), not available.

opciones.texto: All the students attended the class on time despite the fact that the teacher cancelled the session.
opciones.explicacion: It does not express a concessional opposition but a direct effect of lack of space.

bloques.frase: Es ist so kalt, dass ich friere
bloques.explicacion: so + adjective + dass + verb at the end.

bloques.pregunta: What is the correct way of «That's why.» to join two main phrases?

opciones.explicacion: daher = that's why, with the verb in second position.

bloques.pregunta: How is «It's so hot we're going to the pool.» German structure?

opciones.texto: Es ist so heiß, dass wir ins Schwimmbad gehen.
opciones.explicacion: The «so + adjetivo» coraccount announces the consecutive subordinate with «dass» and conjugated verb at the end.

opciones.texto: Es ist so heiß, sodass gehen wir ins Schwimmbad.
opciones.explicacion: «sodass» does not combine with immediate verbal investment in second position.

opciones.texto: Es ist sehr heiß, weil wir ins Schwimmbad gehen.
opciones.explicacion: «weil» expresses cause («Because we're going»), which inverts the logic of the phrase.

intro: Today we are talking about consequences and how to put ideas together in a text. They are the connectors that give a clear argument: cause, consequence and opposition.
